#schema: # The session store (docs/designs/current/DESIGN-coordinator-record-teardown.md):
# the coordinator's record is always its koto session. coordinate-open.sh
# probes at every start, by feature from each subcommand's own `--help`,
# whether this koto lists keys by prefix and imports a session, and refuses a
# start on a koto lacking either (store-unsupported), naming it, before any
# session opens; the record is mode:session-store, never checked at load, so
# the start's probe is the check that runs. The session store's other calls
# (`context exists`, `context remove`, `session list`) are declared above, and
# so is `context list --prefix`. `session import` has one call site, coordinate-open.sh --import,
# which compiles the shipped template (`template compile`, declared above, so
# koto finds the run's template in this host's cache), and passes --from
# always and --trust-template only when the operator gave it.
koto
# The takeover (docs/designs/DESIGN-coordinate-successor-continues.md): when
# the run a start would resume is driven by another Claude session,
# coordinate-open.sh continues it through koto's fence, `koto init --continues
# --supersede --expect-state --carry` (koto 0.28.0 and later). Only a takeover
# makes the call, so the record is mode:takeover, never checked at load; on an
# older koto the opener reads `koto init --help` first and prints
# outcome=refused and reason=koto-too-old with nothing written. It reads a
# successor's predecessor from `koto session hierarchy`, to tell its own
# interrupted takeover from another session's.
koto
